title: The Late Inheritance
premise: When the coffin of Harborline's founder, Augustus Vane, is found empty during a cemetery relocation, insurance investigator Oscar Voss is pulled into a case that unravels seven years of carefully filed secrets—including his own quiet, unspoken love for the coroner's daughter, Maren, who has her own reasons to dig. As Oscar's photographic memory reconstructs the town's buried past, he realizes the empty coffin is a message aimed at him: someone knows what he saw the night Augustus Vane died. The killer is a man Oscar once cleared of arson, now the town's rising power broker, who has spent seven years corrupting the institutions Oscar trusted. In the end, Oscar must choose between the safety of staying invisible and testifying to what he remembers, trapping the killer as the tide finally returns the body—and with it, the truth that gives Oscar, at last, a place to belong.
about_author: Dominic Crane is the pen name of a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent a decade investigating claims in small coastal towns before turning to fiction. They write slow-burn mysteries about memory, complicity, and the places people hide.

chapters.title: The Weight of Empty Ground
chapters.summary: Oscar Voss, POV. During Harborline's cemetery relocation, the founder's coffin comes up light—and empty. Oscar's photographic memory flashes to the night of Vane's funeral seven years ago. The town wants the anomaly buried quietly; the mayor pressures the crew. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine, as Oscar realizes his invisibility is ending.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Secrets
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Oscar revisits his private files and finds a gap: the coroner's report on Vane's death, which he photographed but never fully examined. Maren Delacroix, now deputy coroner, catches him in the records room and demands answers. Their charged, guarded reunion reveals old affection and old wounds. Emotional beat: longing complicated by mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. A partial human remain washes up near the old cannery—too degraded to identify, too fresh to be Vane. Maren's forensic work suggests the body was moved recently. Someone is staging evidence. Emotional beat: her growing certainty that the town's beloved history is a curated lie, and that Oscar is hiding something.

chapters.title: The Man Who Was Cleared
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Councilman Elias Rook—the man Oscar's testimony once cleared of arson—now controls the port expansion Vane opposed. Oscar replays the arson trial in his memory and finds a detail he filed but ignored: Rook's alibi was signed by the same coroner who certified Vane's death. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Small Complicities
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Oscar traces how Rook quietly bought the police chief, the records clerk, and the newspaper editor. His own clean testimony was the keystone. Maren confronts him: he knew something was wrong and chose to stay invisible. Emotional beat: the cost of neutrality named out loud; love against duty sharpened.

chapters.title: The Second Empty Grave
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. The gravedigger who first reported the empty coffin is found drowned—ruled accidental. Maren realizes the killer is deleting the case file person by person, and that she and Oscar are next. She finds a note in her father's old effects: 'Vane knew about the cannery. Ask Oscar what he saw.' Emotional beat: fear turning to fierce protectiveness.

chapters.title: Photographic
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Oscar finally lets his memory of the night Vane died surface fully: he saw Rook at the boathouse, saw the body, and let himself be persuaded he'd seen nothing. He and Maren plan a trap—leak a false version of the evidence through the corrupt clerk. Emotional beat: self-forgiveness beginning; the choice to be seen.

chapters.title: The Trap and the Turn
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. The bait works too well: Rook doesn't take it—he anticipates it, revealing he has a copy of Oscar's own files. He offers Oscar a partnership: silence, money, Maren's safety. Emotional beat: the corrupting power of being known; Oscar must decide whether the man who knows the file better than anyone is himself.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Up
chapters.summary: Oscar and Maren, alternating. At the cannery, Rook comes to destroy the last physical evidence—and finds Oscar waiting, having memorized every detail Rook's plan depended on. The tide uncovers Vane's remains exactly where Oscar's memory said they'd be. Maren records Rook's confession. Emotional beat: climax—memory as weapon, love as courage.

chapters.title: Filed Under Belonging
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Weeks later: Rook convicted, the town's complicity aired, Oscar's testimony public. He burns his private files—not to forget, but to stop hiding. He and Maren walk the relocated cemetery, where Vane's restored headstone reads a truth at last. Emotional beat: resolution—belonging chosen, not inherited; the case closed, the man opened.
